findings.statement: Scope: this is one bounded replay (run run:72cf0e4b91a3, 55 dataset events, 3/3 jobs completed, clink exit status 0, not cancelled; fan-in threshold 5 distinct senders per 3,600,000 ms event-time window; onward max gap 1,800,000 ms). The graph holds 55 transfers, 48 accounts, 35 devices, 14 onward links and exactly 2 fan-in alerts. Everything below holds only for this dataset as this run processed it.

Alert 1, fan_in:A-9278:1794301200000: account A-9278 received 6 transfers from 6 distinct senders in window 1794301200000–1794304800000, totalling 357000 minor units. The contributing transfers are T0002, T0003, T0006, T0010, T0011 and T0012. Amounts vary from 38000 to 89000, and each sender used a different device.

Alert 2, fan_in:A-9895:1794319200000: account A-9895 received 6 transfers from 6 distinct senders in window 1794319200000–1794322800000, totalling 15000 minor units. The contributing transfers are T0035 to T0040. Each is exactly 2500, and each was sent from a different device.

Alert 1's onward route: all 6 contributing transfers have onward links. T0002, T0003 and T0006 link to T0007 (A-9278 to A-5092, 138000), which links to T0008 (A-5092 to A-2897, 135000), which links to T0009 (A-2897 to A-4989, 132000). T0010, T0011 and T0012 link to T0014 (A-9278 to A-5092, 210000), then T0015 (A-5092 to A-2897, 206000), then T0016 (A-2897 to A-4989, 202000). Chains are at most 3 onward links long. Both final transfers, T0009 and T0016, were not passed on, so the money comes to rest at A-4989. The route accounts are A-9278, A-5092, A-2897 and A-4989.

Alert 2's onward route: only 3 of the 6 contributing transfers (T0038, T0039, T0040) link onward, all to a single transfer, T0041 (A-9895 to A-1415, 14000). T0041 was not passed on. T0035, T0036 and T0037 were not passed on either, so in the recorded links those credits stay at A-9895. Chains are at most 1 onward link long. The chain ends are A-1415 and A-9895, and the route accounts are A-9895 and A-1415. A-1415 later sent T0055 (90000 to A-9514, at 1794333900000), but no onward link connects it to T0041, because T0055 falls well outside the 1,800,000 ms gap.

Shared devices on routes, alert 1: device D-568 was used to send every onward transfer on the route, T0007, T0008, T0009, T0014, T0015 and T0016. That means route accounts A-9278, A-5092 and A-2897 all sent from D-568. A-4989 sent no transfers in the dataset.

Shared devices on routes, alert 2: no device was used by two or more of its route accounts. A-9895 sent from D-699, and A-1415 sent from D-785. The only other shared device in the dataset, D-619 (used by A-2952 and A-9652), is not on either alert's route.

What separates the alerts: both show 6 senders and 6 transfers in one hour, but the recorded relationships beneath them differ. (a) Onward depth: alert 1 has a 3-hop onward route along A-9278, A-5092, A-2897 and A-4989, and all of its contributing transfers lead onward. Alert 2 has a single 1-hop link, and only half of its contributing transfers lead onward. (b) Amounts: on alert 1's route, two batches of credits (141500 and 215500) move on as 138000 and 210000, and each later hop is a few thousand smaller. Alert 2 has uniform 2500 credits, and only 14000 moves on. (c) Devices: every hop on alert 1's route was sent from one device, D-568, by three different route accounts. Alert 2's route has no shared device. (d) Downstream alerts: no downstream route account of either alert (A-5092, A-2897, A-4989, A-1415) has its own fan-in alert. So the indicator alone would miss the route behind alert 1.

hypotheses.statement: Alert 1 may be a collection-and-layering pattern: funds gathered at A-9278 and moved quickly through A-5092 and A-2897 to A-4989. If so, the single device D-568 on every hop could mean the three route accounts are operated by one party. The data does not establish this. A shared device is not proof of shared ownership, identity or fraud.

Alert 2 could be benign, for example many small identical payments such as a collection or a split bill, followed by an ordinary later payment. The onward link to T0041 is a timing link only (14000 sent after 7500 of linked credits) and does not show that those specific funds moved on.
The small amount drops at each hop on alert 1's route (3000–4000 minor units) might be fees or retained cuts. Nothing recorded explains them.

unresolved.question: Who controls device D-568, and do A-9278, A-5092 and A-2897 share an owner? The dataset records only device use, not ownership or identity.
What happens to funds at A-4989 and A-1415 after this dataset ends? A-4989 sends nothing in the bounded replay, and events outside it are not visible.
Where did the funds for A-1415's T0055 (90000) come from? A-1415 received only 14000 in the dataset, and account balances and earlier history are not recorded.
Are the onward links value-preserving? The links record only event-time proximity, so it cannot be determined which credits actually funded which debits.
